title: Alerts center UI with badge behavior
objective: The Alerts & Escalation screen per spec FR-62/FR-63 / PRD 18.2: category cards, tabbed escalation queue with premium-at-risk rollup, contextual per-row actions opening workflow dialogs, and the per-user new-alert badge on nav + bell that resets on open.
scope: Route /alerts with ?category= deep-link support (dashboards pre-filter into it)
Category summary cards activating queue tabs
Queue table with flags and contextual Action column
Badge: nav + bell count, reset on Alerts center open
implementation_details: features/alerts/AlertsCenterPage.tsx: CategoryCards row (Escalated 'High-value & stalled', Stalled 'No activity 7+ days' (definition text rendered from tenant thresholds), Overdue, Expiring, SLA Breaches) — click activates matching tab; QueueHeader with rollup 'Premium at risk: {currency} {amount} · {n} quotes'; Tabs All/Escalated/Overdue/Expiring/SLA with counts

AlertsQueueTable: columns ref (monospace), client (product line beneath), broker or 'Direct', premium at risk (right-aligned), stage StatusChip, age (amber/red), owner, flag chips, Action; row click -> /leads/{id} with ?highlightQuote={quoteId} (Lead Detail highlights the alerting quote row — small addition to T-029 QuotesCard reading the param)

Action column: contextual link per alert type — unassigned_lead -> 'Assign & acknowledge' opens AssignDialog (from T-028); overdue_follow_up -> 'Follow up' opens LogFollowUpDialog; executive_escalation/high_value_stalled -> 'Executive review' opens a review dialog (comment + acknowledge, writes follow-up note); completing an action triggers alert refetch (backend targeted re-evaluation clears/downgrades)
Filters: standard bar + owner, product, cover type, region, priority, tenant (internal cross-tenant mode only)

Badge wiring: alertsBadge slice polling GET /alerts/badge (60s interval + on window focus); Sidebar Alerts item and TopBar bell render the count; entering /alerts fires POST /alerts/badge/reset then zeroes the slice

T-043 amendment (docs/ui-remediation/plan.md, AC-082): build every screen part of this task on the shared design-system layer from T-043 — src/ui/src/theme/components.css classes (.qiq-card, .qiq-btn, .qiq-chip, .qiq-table-wrap, .qiq-kpi-*, .qiq-menu) and components/common/Icon.tsx — never ad-hoc inline styling or new CSS files. Before marking IMPLEMENTED, do a side-by-side check against docs/prototype/screenshots/QuoteIQ - Alerts.png at ~1670px: layout regions, card composition, chart types, chip/color semantics must match the prototype (subject to the PRD's documented deviations for this screen, e.g. lead-vs-quote labeling, excluded prototype-only widgets). Record the comparison result in this task's history.

e2e: alerts-center.spec.ts: category card click activates matching tab with counts; queue shows premium-at-risk rollup; 'Assign & acknowledge' on an unassigned lead opens the assign dialog and the alert clears after completion; row click opens Lead Detail with the alerting quote highlighted; badge shows new-alert count, opening the center resets it to zero, and it stays zero for that user after reload while another user still sees their own count

findings.title: Cross-tenant 'tenant' filter omitted — no backend support on the alerts list
findings.detail: implementation_details lists a 'tenant (internal cross-tenant mode only)' filter, but the T-024 ListAlerts endpoint (GET /api/v1/alerts) exposes only tab/ownerUserId/productLineId/coverTypeId/regionId/priority — alerts are strictly active-tenant-scoped via the X-Tenant-Id header (AlertEndpoints.cs TenantScopedGroup). There is no tenant query parameter and no cross-tenant alert aggregation server-side. Implemented owner/product/cover type/region/priority (all backend-supported) and deliberately did NOT invent a cross-tenant tenant filter (CLAUDE.md: do not silently fill gaps). Cross-tenant alert viewing today is via the shell tenant switcher (re-scopes the whole app). Recommended follow-up if a per-list tenant filter is truly required: add a tenant param + cross-tenant aggregation to ListAlerts guarded by the Internal global permission.

findings.title: Filter-bar set follows backend params, not the prototype's Date/Broker/RM
findings.detail: The prototype's Alerts filter bar shows Date Range, Product Line, Broker, RM, Region. The backend ListAlerts supports owner (=RM), product line, cover type, region, priority — no broker or date filter. Implemented the backend-supported set (owner/product/cover/region/priority) per the task's implementation_details rather than the prototype's Date/Broker set. Documented deviation.

findings.title: Executive-review dialog writes a follow-up note; may 422 past Quote Sent
findings.detail: There is no dedicated 'acknowledge alert' backend endpoint, so the Executive-review action (executive_escalation / high_value_stalled) records its required comment via POST /leads/{id}/operations/log-follow-up with a null next-follow-up date (the task specifies it 'writes a follow-up note'). LogFollowUpCommandHandler requires a future next-follow-up date when the lead is open past Quote Sent, so a review on such a lead can return 422 — surfaced inline in the dialog error slot rather than swallowed. Recommended follow-up: either add a dedicated alert-acknowledge/executive-review backend operation, or have the review dialog collect a next-follow-up date when the alerting lead is past Quote Sent.

findings.title: Small additive highlightQuote read on Lead Detail / QuotesCard (T-029)
findings.detail: Per implementation_details ('row click -> /leads/{id} with ?highlightQuote={quoteId} ... small addition to T-029 QuotesCard reading the param'), added a ?highlightQuote= param read in LeadDetailPage and a highlightQuoteId prop on QuotesCard that auto-expands and marks (data-highlighted) the alerting quote row on load. No behavior change when the param is absent. Flagged as the sanctioned small T-029 addition.

findings.title: Per-user badge reset is server-persisted (AC-062)
findings.detail: The new-alert badge is reset by POST /api/v1/alerts/badge/reset, which T-024 persists per user (upserts the caller's last-opened timestamp); GET /api/v1/alerts/badge then counts only alerts created after that per-user timestamp. The frontend zeroes the local Redux slice optimistically on the reset thunk, but correctness across reloads and per-user independence (AC-062) come from the server persistence, not local state — so the badge stays zero for that user after reload while another user still sees their own count.

findings.evaluator_confirmation: CONFIRMED RESOLVED by evaluator re-audit (iteration 2/10, 2026-07-14). Verified against actual files: ExecutiveReviewDialog.tsx renders a required next-follow-up date field when requiresNextFollowUpDate is set, client-side blocks submit when empty (field-error-exec-next-follow-up) or non-future (<= todayIso), and forwards the date via onConfirm(comment, nextFollowUpDate). AlertsCenterPage.beginAction now fetches the lead for the executive-review kind (early return removed) and the dialog gates on actionLead; requiresNextFollowUpDate = deriveLeadReportingCategory(actionLead.statusName) === 'quoted' — the SAME heuristic LogFollowUpDialog uses (both call deriveLeadReportingCategory on the LeadDetailDto statusName). handleExecutiveReviewConfirm forwards the date into logFollowUp(actionLead.id, today, comment, nextFollowUpDate). Not-past case preserved (no date field, null date). The 2 new tests are genuine and non-tautological: the past-Quote-Sent test asserts the date field appears, comment-only submit shows the error AND logFollowUp is NOT called, then a future date calls logFollowUp exactly once with (40, any, comment, futureDate); the not-past test asserts no date field + logFollowUp called with null. Gates re-run by evaluator: typecheck GREEN (exit 0), build GREEN (767 modules, only pre-existing chunk-size advisory), vitest GREEN 89 files/449 tests (+2), alerts suite 28 + AlertsCenterPage 9 all pass, V-070 raw-hex grep over features/alerts clean. Scope containment confirmed: only the 3 frontend files under features/alerts were modified (most-recent mtimes 06:00-06:01, cleanly separated from iteration-1 files); no backend .cs file touched — LogFollowUpCommandHandler remains the source of truth.
findings.resolution: Fixed frontend-only (iteration 2/10), no backend change. beginAction now fetches the lead for the executive-review kind too (removed the early return that skipped the lead prefetch), mirroring the assign/follow-up path. ExecutiveReviewDialog gained a requiresNextFollowUpDate prop and a next-follow-up date field: when the alerting lead's reporting category is Quoted (open past Quote Sent, derived via deriveLeadReportingCategory(actionLead.statusName) === 'quoted' — the same heuristic LogFollowUpDialog/LeadsTable use), the dialog REQUIRES a strictly-future next-follow-up date (client-side validation blocks submit before any backend round-trip) and passes it through onConfirm -> logFollowUp(leadId, today, comment, nextFollowUpDate). When the lead is NOT past Quote Sent, prior behavior is preserved (comment only, null date). handleExecutiveReviewConfirm now uses actionLead.id and forwards the date. The executive-review dialog now gates on actionLead being loaded (like assign/follow-up) so the required-date decision is accurate. Two genuine component tests added to AlertsCenterPage.test.tsx: (a) Quoted-category lead shows+requires the date, blocks submit with logFollowUp NOT called until a future date is provided, then submits with the date (does not dead-end); (b) not-past-Quote-Sent lead has no date field and submits comment-only with a null date. Backend LogFollowUpCommandHandler remains the source of truth.
findings.description: Ruling on the Implementor's F-037-03. The Executive-review action (executive_escalation / high_value_stalled alerts) calls handleExecutiveReviewConfirm -> logFollowUp(leadId, today, comment, null) with a null next-follow-up date. LogFollowUpCommandHandler (LogFollowUpCommandHandler.cs lines 41-54) returns a validation failure (surfaced as 4xx) whenever the lead's current status is in ReportingCategory.Quoted (open past Quote Sent) and NextFollowUpDate is null. This is NOT an edge case for these two alert types: HighValueStalledRule and ExecutiveEscalationRule both fire on leads with quotes — ExecutiveEscalationRule.IsStalled uses StalledQuoteDays for post-quote leads, and the ExecutiveEscalationRule 'expiring' branch requires an OPEN SENT quote (valid_until within the window), which only exists on leads at/past Quote Sent (Quoted category). So the dominant real-world executive-review target — a high-value quote that was sent and then stalled or is expiring — lands squarely on a Quoted-category lead and will hard-fail. The ExecutiveReviewDialog collects only a comment and exposes NO next-follow-up date field, so the reviewer sees the inline error 'A next follow-up date is required while the lead is open past Quote Sent' with no way to satisfy it: the required action path (AC-061: 'contextual actions ... clear/downgrade the alert on completion') dead-ends. Because the affected case is common rather than rare, this is a blocking functional defect, not an acceptable inline-surfaced limitation for this iteration.
findings.evidence: AlertsCenterPage.tsx handleExecutiveReviewConfirm (line 268-282) passes null nextFollowUpDate; ExecutiveReviewDialog.tsx collects only a comment (no date field); LogFollowUpCommandHandler.cs lines 41-54 reject null/non-future NextFollowUpDate when ReportingCategory == Quoted; ExecutiveEscalationRule.cs lines 37-45 (expiring requires an open sent quote) and IsStalled lines 60-70 (StalledQuoteDays for post-quote leads); HighValueStalledRule.cs lines 31-49.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the executive-review path able to complete on Quoted-category leads. Preferred: fetch the lead in beginAction for the executive-review kind (as assign/follow-up already do) and, when the lead's reporting category is Quoted, have ExecutiveReviewDialog require a future next-follow-up date and pass it through to logFollowUp. Acceptable alternatives: always collect an optional next-follow-up date in the review dialog and require it when the backend would demand it; or (best long-term, but out of this frontend task's scope) add a dedicated alert-acknowledge / executive-review backend operation that records the comment without the past-Quote-Sent follow-up constraint — if pursued, raise a backend task rather than blocking here. Add a component test proving the executive-review on a Quoted-category lead collects and submits a next-follow-up date and does not dead-end.

findings.title: AC-062 reload-persistence + multi-user independence is only expressible in e2e, which is describe.fixme
findings.description: The AC-062 guarantee that the badge stays zero for a user across a full reload while another user still sees their own count is a server-persistence property that the frontend unit tests (mocked alertsApi) cannot prove — they can only prove the reset thunk calls the server endpoint and zeroes local state. That end-to-end guarantee is captured in e2e_tests/tests/alerts-center.spec.ts (real body, correct assertions incl. pageA.reload() then badge count 0, plus user B independent) but is currently test.describe.fixme, deferred on T-041 seed data + live stack per the established precedent (dashboard-pipeline/lead-workflow specs). It is backstopped at the integration level by QuoteIQ.Api.Tests AlertEndpointsTests.Badge_ShouldResetToZeroForCallingUserOnly, so this is not blocking — but the browser-level reload-persistence assertion for this exact AC remains unproven in CI until the fixme is lifted. Track un-fixme with T-041.
findings.evidence: alerts-center.spec.ts lines 77-107 (describe.fixme, real assertions); AlertEndpointsTests.cs line 81 Badge_ShouldResetToZeroForCallingUserOnly; alertsBadgeSlice.test.ts (mocked, proves thunk calls server + zeroes local).
findings.suggested_fix: Lift the describe.fixme once T-041 provisions per-category alert conditions and a second badge persona and the compose stack is available; no code change required now.

findings.title: Evaluator rulings on F-037-01/02/04/05 — accepted
findings.description: F-037-01 (no cross-tenant tenant filter): ACCEPTED. The T-024 ListAlerts endpoint (AlertEndpoints.cs) exposes no tenant param and alerts are strictly X-Tenant-Id scoped; inventing a client-side cross-tenant filter would silently fill a backend gap (against CLAUDE.md). Non-blocking; recommended backend follow-up if a per-list tenant filter is truly required. F-037-02 (filter set owner/product/cover/region/priority vs prototype Date/Broker/RM): ACCEPTED. The implemented set matches the backend ListAlerts params; the prototype's Date/Broker filters have no backend support. Documented deviation, non-blocking. F-037-04 (highlightQuote read on Lead Detail/QuotesCard): ACCEPTED as additive + regression-free. QuotesCard.tsx lines 158-169 guard on `highlightQuoteId == null` early-return (no behavior change when the param is absent); the 157 lead+quote vitest tests all pass. F-037-05 (badge reset server-persisted): CONFIRMED ACCURATE. alertsBadgeSlice.ts relies on POST /alerts/badge/reset (resetAlertBadge) for correctness and does not fake per-user state locally; the slice test proves the reset thunk calls the server endpoint and zeroes local state.
